citation_details.title: REVE: A Foundation Model for EEG - Adapting to Any Setup with Large-Scale Pretraining on 25,000 Subjects
citation_details.author: Yassine El Ouahidi, Jonathan Lys, Philipp Thölke, Nicolas Farrugia, B. Pasdeloup, Vincent Gripon, Karim Jerbi, Giulia Lioi
citation_details.abstract: Foundation models have transformed AI by reducing reliance on task-specific data through large-scale pretraining. While successful in language and vision, their adoption in EEG has lagged due to the heterogeneity of public datasets, which are collected under varying protocols, devices, and electrode configurations. Existing EEG foundation models struggle to generalize across these variations, often restricting pretraining to a single setup, resulting in suboptimal performance, in particular under linear probing. We present REVE (Representation for EEG with Versatile Embeddings), a pretrained model explicitly designed to generalize across diverse EEG signals. REVE introduces a novel 4D positional encoding scheme that enables it to process signals of arbitrary length and electrode arrangement. citation_details.title: EEG Foundation Challenge: From Cross-Task to Cross-Subject EEG Decoding
citation_details.author: Bruno Aristimunha, Dung Truong, Pierre Guetschel, Seyed Yahya Shirazi, Isabelle Guyon, Alexandre R. Franco, M. Milham, Aviv Dotan, S. Makeig, Alexandre Gramfort, Jean-Rémi King, Marie-Constance Corsi, P. Valdés-Sosa, Amit Majumdar, Alan Evans, Terrence J. Sejnowski, O. Shriki, Sylvain Chevallier, Arnaud Delorme
citation_details.abstract: Current electroencephalogram (EEG) decoding models are typically trained on small numbers of subjects performing a single task. Here, we introduce a large-scale, code-submission-based competition comprising two challenges. First, the Transfer Challenge asks participants to build and test a model that can zero-shot decode new tasks and new subjects from their EEG data. Second, the Psychopathology factor prediction Challenge asks participants to infer subject measures of mental health from EEG data. For this, we use an unprecedented, multi-terabyte dataset of high-density EEG signals (128 channels) recorded from over 3,000 child to young adult subjects engaged in multiple active and passive tasks. We provide several tunable neural network baselines for each of these two challenges, including a simple network and demographic-based regression models. Developing models that generalise across tasks and individuals will pave the way for ML network architectures capable of adapting to EEG data

citation_details.title: DIVER-1 : Deep Integration of Vast Electrophysiological Recordings at Scale
citation_details.author: Danny Dongyeop Han, Yonghyeon Gwon, Ahhyun Lucy Lee, Taeyang Lee, Seongjin Lee, Jubin Choi, Sebin Lee, J. Bang, Seungju Lee, David Keetae Park, Shinjae Yoo, Chun Kee Chung, Jiook Cha
citation_details.abstract: Unifying the vast heterogeneity of brain signals into a single foundation model is a longstanding challenge in neuroscience. Yet, even as large-scale pretraining becomes feasible, the field lacks principled guidance on how to scale electrophysiological foundation models under realistic data and compute constraints. We present the first systematic scaling law analysis spanning both EEG and iEEG, and uncover a distinct data-constrained characteristic. citation_details.title: CoMET: A Contrastive-Masked Brain Foundation Model for Universal EEG Representation
citation_details.author: Ang Li, Zikai Wang, Liuyin Yang, Zhenyu Wang, Tianheng Xu, Honglin Hu, Marc M. Van Hulle
citation_details.abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) is a non-invasive technique for recording brain activity, widely used in brain-computer interfaces, clinic, and healthcare. Traditional EEG deep models typically focus on specific dataset and task, limiting model size and generalization. Recently, self-supervised brain foundation models have emerged and been applied to various downstream tasks. Nevertheless, these models still have limitations: current SOTA models typically rely on masked reconstruction strategy; however, EEG features of adjacent channels are highly correlated, which causes the pre-training to overly focus on low-dimensional signal-similarity features in local regions and neglect the global discriminative patterns vital for downstream tasks. citation_details.title: Healthy Brain Network (HBN) EEG - Release 4
citation_details.author: Seyed Yahya Shirazi, Alexandre Franco, Maurício Scopel Hoffmann, Nathalia B. Esper, Dung Truong, Arnaud Delorme, Michael Milham, Scott Makeig
citation_details.abstract: The Healthy Brain Network (HBN) EEG Release 6 dataset comprises high-resolution electroencephalogram recordings from 134 children and adolescents (ages 5-21 years) performing six distinct cognitive and perceptual tasks, including resting state, passive viewing tasks (surround suppression, movie watching), and active tasks (contrast change detection, sequence learning, symbol search). The dataset includes behavioral responses, hierarchical event descriptors for systematic meta-analysis, and psychopathology measures (P-Factor, Attention, Internalization, Externalization) derived from the Child Behavior Checklist, providing a rich resource for investigating neural correlates of typical and atypical development. This release is part of a larger HBN initiative involving >3000 participants.

citation_details.title: NeuralBench: A Unifying Framework to Benchmark NeuroAI Models
citation_details.author: Hubert J. Banville, Stéphane d’Ascoli, Simon Dahan, Jérémy Rapin, Marlène Careil, Yohann Benchetrit, Jarod L'evy, S. Panchavati, Antoine Ratouchniak, Mingfang Zhang, Elisa Cascardi, K. Begany, Teon L Brooks, Jean-Rémi King
citation_details.abstract: Deep learning and large public datasets have recently catalyzed the proliferation of AI models for processing brain recordings. However, systematically evaluating these models remains a challenge: not only do the preprocessing pipelines, training and finetuning approaches largely vary across studies, but their downstream evaluation is often limited to small sets of tasks and/or datasets. Here, we present NeuralBench: a unified framework for benchmarking AI models of brain activity. We accompany this framework with NeuralBench-EEG v1.0 -- a large EEG benchmark that includes 36 electroencephalography (EEG) tasks and 14 deep learning architectures, and is evaluated on 94 datasets accessed through a standardized interface. citation_details.title: Q-DIVER: Integrated Quantum Transfer Learning and Differentiable Quantum Architecture Search with EEG Data
citation_details.author: J. Park, Yeong-Duk Park, Jiook Cha
citation_details.venue: 2026 International Conference on Quantum Communications, Networking, and Computing (QCNC)
citation_details.abstract: Integrating quantum circuits into deep learning pipelines remains challenging due to heuristic design limitations. We propose Q-DIVER, a hybrid framework combining a largescale pretrained EEG encoder (DIVER-1) with a differentiable quantum classifier. Unlike fixed-ansatz approaches, we employ Differentiable Quantum Architecture Search to autonomously discover task-optimal circuit topologies during end-to-end finetuning. On the PhysioNet Motor Imagery dataset, our quantum classifier achieves predictive performance comparable to classical multi-layer perceptrons (Test F1: 63.49 %) while using approximately 50 × fewer task-specific head parameters (2.10 M vs. 105.02M). These results validate quantum transfer learning as a parameter-efficient strategy for high-dimensional biological signal processing.

citation_details.title: EegCNR: A Novel Feature for Attention Estimation From EEG
citation_details.author: Asif M S, S. K., A. P. Vinod
citation_details.venue: 2025 Asia Pacific Signal and Information Processing Association Annual Summit and Conference (APSIPA ASC)
citation_details.abstract: Attention is one of the most crucial cognitive factors for a high-quality living and survival for a person. Electroencephalogram (EEG)-based attention estimation has been explored by researchers as a promising approach for non-invasive monitoring of a person's mental focus and vigilance. In this paper, we present a novel approach for EEG-based attention quantification using an image contrast feature, generalized Contrast-to-Noise Ratio (gCNR) adopted from the domain of biomedical ultrasound. The work validates the effectiveness of gCNR in attention quantification, using the EEG data collected from 14 healthy subjects using the proposed experimental paradigm. The performance of the gCNR feature is further tested on Healthy-Brain Network (HBN)-R1, a larger open-source dataset of 136 subjects. citation_details.title: EEG-Based Mental Health Analysis and Classification for Healthy Brain Network(HBN)
citation_details.author: Ayush Nikhara, Arnav Arya, S. S, Daehan Won
citation_details.venue: 2025 Innovations in Power and Advanced Computing Technologies (i-PACT)
citation_details.abstract: Electroencephalography(EEG) signals are important indicators of brain activity and states of mind. This study conducts an in-depth exploration of the Healthy Brain Network EEG Dataset, presenting key findings and insights derived from the analysis. The significant features extracted are mean, standard deviation, variance, power spectral densities (Delta, Theta, Alpha, Beta, and Gamma), entropy, wavelet energy, and the Hurst exponent. Early results indicate that Beta and Gamma power components of greater frequency have high correlations with cognitive processing, whereas lower frequency bands like Delta and Theta are associated with relaxation and sleep. Entropy and wavelet energy also play a part in discriminating between active and passive brain states. citation_details.title: Neuroelectromagnetic Data Archive and Repository: Open-source platform analysis
citation_details.author: Tracy Brandmeyer, Anna Riggs, Viraaj Reddi, Hayley Sullivan, Choonhan Youn, Subhashini Sivagnanam, Kenneth Yoshimoto, Russell A. Poldrack, Nell Hardcastle, Christopher Markiewicz, Amitava Majumdar, Yahya Shirazi, Dung Truong, Scott Makeig, A. Delorme
citation_details.abstract: Open data infrastructures are rapidly reshaping the landscape of neuroscience by enabling greater reproducibility through transparency, reusability, and collaboration, thus providing a foundation for sustainable and scalable scientific progress. This paper presents a systematic audit of the Neuroelectromagnetic Data Archive and Repository (NEMAR), a platform supporting the sharing and reuse of EEG, MEG, and iEEG datasets standardized through the Brain Imaging Data Structure (BIDS) format. Drawing on a detailed analysis of over 300 publicly available datasets, we assess the composition, metadata quality, and population coverage of data in NEMAR. Our findings reveal significant momentum in data sharing practices, particularly in EEG, and highlight key challenges, including inconsistent metadata, underrepresentation of clinical populations, and variable adherence to data standards. These insights highlight the importance of targeted support for policy and cultural development to ensure open repositories like NEMAR are not only accessible but also equitable, reusable, and scientifically robust.

citation_details.title: 5D Conscious State Test Suite: Reproducibility Package for The Geometry of Conscious States
citation_details.author: Spencer Howie
citation_details.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
citation_details.abstract: Python test suite and intermediate results accompanying Howie (2026e), "The Geometry of Conscious States: A Five-Dimensional Framework." Self-contained reproducibility package for every numeric result in the paper: every figure, table, and cited value reproduces from the deposited per-subject feature JSONs by running `scripts/run_all.sh --stage analyze` on a clean checkout. Five EEG datasets (~314 subjects after QC), processed with the CAR-harmonized v1.2 pipeline and analyzed under the 5D state-geometry framework: Sleep (ANPHY-Sleep, OSF: thsqg) — n = 28; sleep exit(W to N3) Cambridge propofol (Chennu et al. archive) — n = 19; propofol exit (Baseline to Moderate) DS005620 propofol (OpenNeuro ds005620) — n = 20; light-sedation hybrid - SRM (OpenNeuro ds003775) — n = 111; normative healthy-adult baseline HBN (OpenNeuro ds005505) — n = 136; rel_alpha swap verification (EC vs EO) What's included: Pipelines (raw EEG to per-subject 5D features): reprocess_car_local.py: Sleep + Cambridge CAR + I_Preprocessing ds003775_reprocess.py: SRM normative baseline ds005620_reprocess.py: light-sedation reprocessing hbn_reader.py / hbn_reprocess.py: HBN developmental normative phi5_swap_committed.py: rel_alpha swap verification driver Analyses (committed feature JSONs to canonical numbers): trajectory_geometry.py: group-mean 5D vectors, trajectory magnitudes, inter-paradigm angles trajectory_stats.py: per-subject trajectory statistics, bootstrap CIs, label-permutation tests, leave-one-out sensitivity angular_dispersion.py: per-subject trajectory dispersion dispersion_pathway_figure.py: dispersion / pathway visualization weighted_geomean_analysis.py: Fisher LDA weights vs equal-weights comparison via log-space LDA swap_effect_sizes.py: rel_alpha-vs-I_P channel-swap per-cohort effect sizes (Cohen's paired d_z, four-cohort composite) Outputs: outputs/<cohort>_5d_car_data.json: per-subject 5D featurevectors for each cohort outputs/canonical/: every result cited in the paper as CSV / JSON / log; verify_outputs.py diffs a fresh run against this outputs/figures/: PNG and SVG figure outputs Series-wide compute primitives (_framework_core/) shared byte-identically with the empirical-paper deposits: pairwise Granger causality, GC matrix construction, transitive closure, spectral radius, all five Phi5 channels. I_R operationalization: the canonical normalized spectral radius rho(W) / rho_max of the thresholded Granger-causality graph. Reproducibility: run_all.sh runs the full pipeline (preprocess to analyze to verify); accepts --datasets and --analysis filters for partial re-runs verify_outputs.py reports "OK -- all canonical values reproduce within tolerance" on a clean unzip environment.yml (conda) and requirements.txt (pip fallback) pin dependencies manifests/ tracks every QC'd subject ID across the five datasets Data sources (downloaded separately, not redistributed): ANPHY-Sleep (OSF: thsqg) Cambridge propofol (Chennu et al. archive; access details indatasets/manifest.md) OpenNeuro ds005620 (light-sedation paradigm) OpenNeuro ds003775 (resting-state normative cohort) OpenNeuro ds005505 (HBN developmental cohort) License: MIT.

citation_details.title: 5D Conscious State Test Suite: Reproducibility Package for The Geometry of Conscious States
citation_details.author: Spencer Howie
citation_details.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
citation_details.abstract: Standalone reproducibility package for the manuscript "The Geometry of Conscious States: A Five-Dimensional Framework" (Howie, 2026, Zenodo, forthcoming). The code and committed feature data regenerate every numeric result cited in that manuscript — group-mean state vectors and magnitudes, inter-paradigm angles, per-subject trajectory dispersion statistics, the pooled-baseline Φ_ref calibration (n=67), and the equal-weighted versus Fisher-weighted geometric-mean comparison — from five publicly available EEG datasets: ANPHY Sleep (OpenNeuro ds003768, n=28) — endogenous acute exit Cambridge propofol (n=19) — pharmacological acute exit ds005620 light propofol sedation (n=28) — partial pharmacological exit ds003775 SRM normative (n=111) — pooled-baseline anchor ds005505 HBN (n=136) — eyes-open / eyes-closed developmental contrast used in the channel-substitution audit Running bash scripts/run_all.sh --stage analyze from the committed feature JSONs reproduces every canonical output; python scripts/verify_outputs.py numerically checks each of the twenty pinned values against the frozen reference in outputs/canonical/paper5_numbers.csv. Raw BIDS preprocessing (CAR re-reference, epoching, feature extraction) is also included under pipelines/ and is invocable if users want to replicate from raw data. The composite implemented is the equal-weighted geometric mean of five channels — interaction asymmetry, organizational specificity (1 − H_norm), inverse memory depth (1 − I_M), recursive integration, and relative alpha power — with the Consciousness Index reported as 100·Φ₅/(Φ₅ + Φ_ref). Canonical Φ_ref = 0.716. The implementation lives in analyses/_common.py. Full directory layout, dataset provenance, and per-number output mapping are documented in the deposit's README.md and MANIFEST.md.
